title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: W is a basic localizer (localisateur fondamental) in (Cat), Hot(W) = W^{-1}(Cat). For a small category A, i_A : A^ -> (Cat) sends a presheaf to its category of elements, W_A = i_A^{-1}(W), and Hot_A(W) = W_A^{-1}A^. On the previous page Grothendieck wants Corollary 2: Hot(W) has finite products and (Cat) -> Hot(W) and A^ -> Hot(W) preserve them. He reduces this to showing that Hom_{Hot_A}(X, prod Y_j) -> prod Hom_{Hot_A}(X, Y_j) is bijective.

Surjectivity: represent the components as roofs X -> Y_j' <- Y_j with Y_j -> Y_j' in W_A. Take f = (f_j) : X -> prod Y_j'. This works provided prod Y_j -> prod Y_j' is in W_A, i.e. provided W_A is stable under finite products.

This page opens: 'C'est le cas si A catégorie test stricte, plus généralement si elle est totalement W-asphérique.' It then states a lemma with equivalent conditions for A in (Cat):
- (i) A is totally W-aspherical: A is W-aspherical and products a×b of representables are W-aspherical, i.e. the diagonal A -> A×A is W-aspherical.
- (ii) W_A is stable under finite products.
- (ii bis) if f : X -> Y is in W_A and Z is in A^, then f×id_Z is in W_A.
- (iii) A^ -> Hot_A commutes with finite products.
- (iv) A^ -> Hot_A(W) commutes with finite products.
A margin diagram sketches the implications (i)⇒(ii), (ii)⇔(iii), and so on, with 'vérification facile'. He postpones the lemma ('on reviendra à ce lemme tantôt'), assumes (ii), and gets surjectivity.

Injectivity: let f, g : X ⇉ Y' with α : Y = prod Y_j -> Y' in W. Suppose that for each j there are β_j : Y_j -> Y_j' in W and φ_j : Y' -> Y_j' with β_j p_j = φ_j α and φ_j f ≃ φ_j g (homotopic). Set β = prod β_j : Y -> Y'' := prod Y_j' and φ = (φ_j). The next page concludes: β ∈ W by (ii), φα = β, and φf ~ φg, hence γ(f) = γ(g).

The next page then proves the lemma: (ii)⇔(ii bis) trivially; (ii bis) reduces, by locality over Z, to Z = a representable; (i)⇒(ii bis); and, if A is aspherical, (ii bis)⇒(i) by taking f : a -> e. So (i) ⇔ (ii) + A aspherical.

Purpose: the W-relative version of the theory of strict test categories, namely that A^ -> Hot commutes with finite products iff A is totally aspherical. This is used to show that Hot(W) has finite products preserved by the localization functors.
errors: As first stated, the lemma lists (i)–(iv) as equivalent. Grothendieck himself finds on the next page that (i) ⇔ (ii) only together with asphericity of A. So (ii)/(iii) do not imply (i) without that hypothesis.

(iv) can recover asphericity only if 'finite products' includes the empty product (A must map to the point in Hot(W)). (iii) does not seem to give it, since the terminal object of A^ should stay terminal in W_A^{-1}A^. So (iii) and (iv) are probably not equivalent in general, and the lemma's list needs adjusting.

The injectivity argument assumes three things that are not justified on this page. First, morphisms of W_A^{-1}A^ are represented by roofs X -> Y' <- Y with the wrong-way arrow in W. Second, equality of morphisms in the localization is witnessed by maps φ_j and a homotopy relation φ_j f ≃ φ_j g. Third, homotopies are compatible with products. These hold with a cylinder/interval or a model structure (Cisinski) but are not proved here.
In the injectivity setup the β_j are chosen independently for each j. One must check that a single Y' and α can be used for all j, which is fine since α is fixed beforehand.

ideas.what: Equivalence between total W-asphericity of A, stability of W_A under finite products, and preservation of finite products by A^ -> Hot_A(W), relative to an arbitrary basic localizer W
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, absolute case W = weak equivalences); developed relative to localizers by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (strict and totally aspherical test categories), absolute case; the W-relative form appears in Maltsiniotis' and Cisinski's expositions

ideas.what: Existence of finite products in Hot(W) and their preservation by (Cat) -> Hot(W) and A^ -> Hot(W), proved via a calculus of roofs and homotopies in A^
ideas.modern_name: Localization functors preserving finite products / homotopy category of a model category with products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Quillen model categories); in the localizer setting, Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Probably implicit in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; unsure of the exact location

ideas.what: Remark (next page) that the argument would extend to infinite products if W_A were stable under infinite products
ideas.modern_name: Stability of weak equivalences under infinite products

deep.surprise_reason: This is the W-relative version of the strict test category / total asphericity criterion. It is already in Pursuing Stacks for the absolute case and was systematized for arbitrary basic localizers by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski. The page is a working draft with a self-corrected lemma; nothing new for specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line after the conditions likely reads 'On en reviendra à ce lemme tantôt. Pour le moment, on suppose vérifié (ii) [d'où la] surjectivité de (*)' rather than 'On se ramène à ce lemme ... il suffit vérifier (ii)'.
The left margin note likely reads 'vérification facile [si A asphérique ...]' with implication arrows. It records the diagram (i)⇒(ii)⇔(iii)⇒... rather than the bracket as transcribed.
Opening line: 'C'est le cas si A catégorie-test stricte' — the word 'test' appears to be attached/kept rather than struck.
In the diagram, the struck annotation next to Y'_j is '= Y' ⨿_Y Y_j' (a pushout), consistent with the transcription.
